chunks: And from him, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Baḥr, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the takbir in al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā. He said: Begin and pronounce one takbir, then recite; then after the recitation pronounce five takbirs, then perform rukuʿ with the seventh. Then stand and recite, then pronounce four takbirs, then perform rukuʿ with the fifth.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: four additional takbirs in the second rakʿah
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: the pronouncing of Allahu Akbar in the ritual prayer
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: the ʿEid of sacrifice, referring to ʿEid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: the ʿEid of breaking the fast, referring to ʿEid al-Fiṭr
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the recitation performed in the prayer
key_terms.بِالسَّابِعَةِ: with the seventh takbir, meaning the rukuʿ follows it in the first rakʿah
key_terms.بِالْخَامِسَةِ: with the fifth takbir, meaning the rukuʿ follows it in the second rakʿah
key_terms.خَمْسَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: five additional takbirs after the recitation in the first rakʿah

ai.seo_question: How are the takbirs performed in the salat of ʿEid al-Fiṭr and ʿEid al-Aḍḥā according to Imam al-Ṣadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of takbir in the salat of the two ʿEids, al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā. It sets out the sequence of recitation and takbirs in the two rakʿahs, making it a jurisprudential report on the structure of the ʿEid prayer.
